header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Time: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jon Park (Redwood Platform), Marcus Allen (Datawise ML), Leah Ortiz (Datawise Infra), Dina Roberts (Datawise Head of AI), Samir Khan (Datawise Security)
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review INT8 and FP8 quantization experiment results. Redwood shared updated perf numbers; customer walked through QA concerns (small regressions on summarization and numeric fidelity). Agreed next steps: share full logs/spreadsheet, customer to run eval suite, schedule KMS/VPC deep dive. Action items captured.
topics:
1) Perf deltas: INT8 vs FP8 (throughput and latency)
2) Quality impact: regressions observed on customer QA set (summarization, numeric exactness)
3) Kernel/compilation tweaks and alternate quant paths
4) Security/compliance: KMS, audit logs, on-prem constraints
5) Next steps / scheduling
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Marcus (Customer): Hey, Marcus here.
[00:14] Leah: Leah here.
[00:16] Dina: Dina on.
[00:20] Alex: Cool, so agenda — quick perf review, quality hits, kernel experiments, and then next steps. Priya do you want to jump in with the numbers?
[00:32] Priya (Redwood SE): Yeah sure. So we re-ran the INT8 and FP8 bench on the 8xA100 pool, same model sharding. Overall tokens/sec improved ~1.8x on INT8 vs fp16 baseline and FP8 shows about 2.3x, p50 lat drop ~18% INT8, ~27% FP8. p95 latency for long sequences saw slightly larger variance for FP8, sometimes spiking.
[01:05] Marcus: Ok, numbers look good. When you say spiking at p95, is that transient or consistent? We saw a couple of failures in the eval set.
[01:20] Priya: More like intermittent, seems correlated with longer context and KV cache pressure. We're seeing a kernel fallback path in FP8 in some cases that adds serialization, need to triage.
[01:45] Jon (Redwood): Also worth noting we tested two compilation kernels — default and nv-custom-quant. NV-custom had better steady throughput for FP8 but had slightly higher memory overhead.
[02:10] Dina: The customer QA flagged summarization degradations — about 3–5% of outputs were shorter or lost numeric tokens. How severe is that expected to be with FP8?
[02:30] Priya: That's expected in the tight quantization budgets — FP8 can sometimes reduce numeric fidelity, especially with models that weren't finetuned for low precision. INT8 tended to be safer on those examples, but you lose some throughput.
[03:00] Marcus: Do we have sample diffs? We need side-by-side examples to show stakeholders.
[03:10] Alex: Yes, we'll upload a diffs CSV and the raw inputs/outputs to the bucket — link will be in the spreadsheet.
[03:25] Samir (Security): On the security front, any differences with FP8/INT8 in terms of logs, or is this purely runtime? Also want to confirm KMS integration will not be affected.
[03:38] Priya: No change to KMS; quantization is model execution only. We will still record audit events per request. If you want, we can show how logs look with tokens and op-level timings.
[03:55] Leah: Great. On deployment: we're leaning to Dedicated for predictable perf, but want to validate FP8 before we commit. If FP8 regresses on our top-traffic prompts, that could push us to INT8 + more nodes.
[04:20] Priya: That tradeoff is exactly what Redwood Optimize is designed to help quantify — cost per 1M tokens vs SLO hit rate. We'll put some sample scenarios in the sheet.
[04:40] Marcus: One other question — did you test cold-start behavior? We saw higher token latency on first few requests in FP8 runs.
[04:52] Jon: We instrumented cold vs warm; cold warm differences were amplified for FP8 due to kernel initialization. Warm steady-state is fine. We have a patch to reduce initialization time but need to test at scale.
[05:15] Dina: Ok. Can you summarize the concrete deltas we should present to execs? Like expected cost savings for FP8 versus quality risk?
[05:30] Alex: Yes — high level: FP8 gives ~25–30% extra throughput versus INT8 in our bench which roughly maps to ~20% cost reduction after memory and instance packing. But quality regressions on your eval are non-zero; INT8 is more conservative: ~15–18% throughput gains over fp16 with fewer regressions. We'll quantify in the spreadsheet.
[06:00] Marcus: On the regressions, we care about two classes: 1) hallucinated numerics and 2) truncation in summaries. If we can get a clear list of inputs that fail, we can try prompt/temperature workarounds.
[06:20] Priya: Agreed — please give us the top 100 failing prompts and we'll try targeted mitigation: input normalization, tokenization fixes, or hybrid mode where critical prompts use INT8.
[06:35] Marcus: Hybrid mode seems interesting. Is it something Redwood supports at routing level?
[06:42] Jon: Yes, routing policies can send particular route keys to INT8 pools while others go to FP8. That is part of the smart routing features.
[06:55] Leah: About kernels — any plan to upstream the nv-custom-quant or is it internal?
[07:03] Priya: It's a Redwood-optimized compilation path that picks different matmul kernels and dot-product precision; some pieces are vendor-specific. We'll document which kernels we used.
[07:20] Marcus: Can you share the exact software stack — runtimes, CUDA, cuDNN versions so we can mirror?
[07:26] Alex: Yes that's in the sheet: pytorch-2.1, cuda 12.2, cuBLAS 12.x, custom redwood runtime v1.9.2.
[07:40] Dina: Any known incompatibilities with our on-prem GPU fleet? We run a mix of A10G and A100.
[07:48] Jon: A10G tends to show lower absolute throughput; quant kernels behave slightly differently. We should run a short baseline on your A10G fleet — Leah can share access.
[08:05] Leah: I'll arrange access to a staging node for a short run.
[08:10] Marcus: Quick digression — competitor question: we looked at VendorX's FP8 demo, they claimed smaller regressions — how much is this model-specific?
[08:22] Priya: It's often model and data specific; VendorX might have done extra calibration or finetune. Our recommendation: try calibration + small finetune if regression rate is unacceptable.
[08:40] Alex: OK, any other items on quality?
[08:45] Dina: I want to confirm metrics we'll use: precision on numerics, ROUGE-L for summaries, and a manual severity label for customer-impacting outputs.
[08:55] Marcus: Agreed. We'll produce that in the eval run.
[09:05] Priya: One more note on memory — FP8 reduced model footprint enabling larger batch packing; but on some runs we hit memory fragmentation leading to unexpected oom and then fallback to slower kernels. We're working on defragmentation heuristics.
[09:30] Marcus: That explains intermittent failures.
[09:36] Alex: We'll include memory heatmaps in the log bundle.
[09:45] [---skipping to mid-call discussion---]
[22:12] Priya: Ran an additional set of runs with early KV-cache warmup; it reduced the p95 spikes by about 12% for FP8 in steady state. Not perfect but helps.
[23:05] Marcus: Did you see any change in quality with the warmup?
[23:12] Priya: No direct quality change — warmup is performance behavior only.
[24:00] Jon: We also tried a hybrid packing ratio where we reserve some slots for high-fidelity responses on INT8 nodes and pack statistically less for FP8. That dropped cost slightly but reduced regressions.
[26:30] Dina: For the exec summary, can you provide two scenarios: conservative (INT8 primary) and aggressive (FP8 primary with selective fallback)?
[26:45] Alex: We'll produce both in the spreadsheet with cost curves and SLO impact.
[28:10] Samir (Security): Quick note on KMS — if we go private deployment, we need to ensure decryption happens in customer VPC/hsm; is that supported?
[28:20] Jon: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM patterns — we have docs and a checklist. We'll set up a call with infra to walk it through.
[28:40] Leah: Can you also surface audit log retention and token-level tracing? That's a security ask from our GRC.
[28:50] Alex: We'll include retention options in the doc.
[30:05] [Noise / crosstalk].
[33:00] Marcus: Any blockers on Redwood's side to run the customer's evals?
[33:10] Priya: No blockers; just need the eval set and sample inputs. Once we have those, we'll run FP8 calibration + INT8 baseline and return a diff report.
[33:30] Marcus: Great. Also please include which prompts we should route to INT8 as a sample hybrid policy.
[33:40] Priya: We'll propose a routing rule set based on prompt fingerprints and detected numeric tokens.
[34:05] Alex: Ok, to recap next steps — we'll upload spreadsheet and logs, Priya will run kernel variant tests, Marcus will run eval and share regressions, Leah to share staging access and KMS config, schedule deep-dive.
[34:25] Dina: Sounds good.
[34:30] Alex: Any final questions?
[34:35] Marcus: No, thanks everyone.
[34:40] Alex: Thanks all, talk soon.
[34:46] [meeting ends]
